subject: Re: Trial onramp & environment choice — Ava Health
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Megan Lee <megan@avahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Trial onramp: success criteria & environment options

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about Ava Health's use case and evaluation priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the trial planning phase.

High-level objective:
- Validate Redwood's inference for clinical summarization workflows (PHI-containing notes) so your product team can assess latency, throughput, and accuracy/regression against your prompt set.

Success criteria (as discussed):
- Functional: model output passes your 12 prompt test-cases with >= 95% acceptance across accuracy/formatting checks.
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for 512-token requests under expected batch sizes.
- Stability: no more than 1% error rate (timeouts/500s) during 1-hour sustained test window.
- Security/Compliance: environment must support BAA and either private VPC connectivity or equivalent isolation controls; audit logs available.

Estimated evaluation footprint:
- Daily traffic during trial: 20–50 concurrent sessions, ~10k tokens/day initially (scale to 50k tokens/day during stress window).
- Trial length proposal: 4 weeks of active evaluation (1 week onboarding + 3 weeks tests/measurements), flexible depending on security approvals.

Environment options (pros/cons):
1) Hosted (Redwood API)
   - Pros: fastest to start, minimal ops. Good for feature-level validation and early tuning.
   - Cons: not ideal if PHI must remain inside your VPC; limited network isolation.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved dedicated nodes in Redwood-managed infra)
   - Pros: predictable performance, dedicated capacity, faster than full VPC.
   - Cons: still requires data handling agreement; better for teams that can tolerate vendor-hosted compute.
3) VPC/private deployment (preferred for PHI)
   - Pros: full network isolation, customer-managed ingress/egress, KMS support.
   - Cons: longer lead time (network approvals, provisioning), requires firewall/peering work on your side.

Recommendation (initial): Start with a short "safety-on" hosted validation (non-PHI test vectors) to confirm infra and prompt integration immediately, while we run the approvals and provisioning for a VPC trial for PHI workloads. If your security team is comfortable, we can provision a VPC trial as the canonical evaluation environment.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Please confirm whether Ava wants us to pursue VPC provisioning as the default path or if a dedicated sandbox would be acceptable.
- Share the security contact(s) — network lead + InfoSec reviewer — so we can schedule a 30–45m tech alignment call (we'll include network checklist).
- I'll attach a short success-criteria workbook + network requirements PDF for your review (attached).

Attachments: AVA_POC_success_criteria.xlsx; network_requirements.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on another call to walk through tradeoffs.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
From: Megan Lee <megan@avahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@avahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial onramp: success criteria & environment options

Thanks Rishi — very helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- PHI: We do expect to evaluate with real PHI-ish records (de-identified + limited PHI) during the trial; therefore VPC or on-prem options are preferred.
- Compliance: We will need a BAA and a copy of your latest SOC 2 Type II report. Please confirm both are available.
- Timeline: our InfoSec lead (Tom) needs to review the network requirements before we commit to provisioning. I've CC'd Tom — Tom, can you share your availability next week for a quick review?

If VPC is going to introduce >2 week delay, we may consider running an initial hosted smoke test (redacted data) to validate integration.

Also: who at Redwood will own the network setup and the firewall rule requests? Please provide a single point-of-contact so we can route the approvals internally.

Thanks,
Megan

Megan Lee
Product Manager, Ava Health
megan@avahealth.com | +1 646-555-0134
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Megan Lee <megan@avahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial onramp: success criteria & environment options

Great — quick answers:

- BAA and SOC 2: Yes. We have a standard BAA we can execute and I'll loop Laura on the SOC2 artifacts; I've included a link to our SOC2 report in the related links above for preliminary review.
- Network ownership: Ben Carter will be the procurement/engops lead on our side and point for firewall/peering coordination; Laura will own the compliance docs and the SOC2 handoff. I'll be the technical lead for integration and tuning.
- Timeline expectation: from experience, VPC provisioning + legal approvals tends to be ~2–4 weeks depending on your internal SLAs. If you want to start sooner we can run a hosted smoke test with redacted data (no PHI) the same week.

Proposed plan (two-track):
A) Immediate (week 0): hosted smoke test (non-PHI) — validate integration, prompt formatting, and basic latency readings.
B) Parallel (weeks 1–3): legal & security reviews -> VPC provisioning -> network validation.
C) Evaluation (week 4): run PHI-enabled tests in the VPC (after BAA and firewall rules in place) and measure against success criteria.

Can you introduce Tom to Ben and Laura so we can get the firewall checklist and legal review started? Also, please confirm preferred kickoff window next week (we're available Tue/Wed afternoon PT).

—
Rishi

Subject: Re: Trial onramp: success criteria & environment options — proposed runway and owners

Megan / Tom — thanks for the quick responses. I've pulled together a pragmatic onramp runway and assigned owners so we can move from call to execution. I've attached the one-page onramp plan. Key dates are below (proposed):

- Week 0 (kickoff): 30-min intro + scope confirmation (target: Tue 24 Jul, 10am PT)
- Week 1: Legal (BAA) & InfoSec review; network checklist completed by Tom; firewall rule request submitted to your infra team
- Week 2: VPC provisioning & peering setup (our infra team + your cloud ops)
- Week 3: Model tuning and sample-run — run the 12 prompt test set, measure p95 latencies, gather logs
- Week 4: PHI-enabled evaluation (in VPC) and success criteria signoff; final decision on production path (Hosted/Dedicated/VPC)

Action owners:
- Ben Carter (Redwood): procurement, contract coordination, schedule owner
- Rishi Malhotra (Redwood): technical lead — integration, prompt tuning, test execution
- Laura Bennett (Redwood): compliance owner — SOC2 artifacts, BAA coordination
- Tom Blake (Ava): network owner — firewall rules and peering approvals
- Megan Lee (Ava): product validation owner — acceptance and test signoff

We expect no-cost trial usage for the evaluation window; if you want reserved capacity we can quote dedicated nodes after success.

Attachments: AVA_POC_onramp_plan.xlsx
Related hubspot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/RDW-2387

Please confirm the kickoff time (Tue 24 Jul 10am PT) or propose an alternate and we'll lock the calendar. Looking forward to getting started.

Best,
